text:
maria (partnerships): Heads up — ACME's marketplace team flagged a problem with our published images: kernel module signatures don't match their signing policy on their private registry. They want either a pinned driver/cuda combo + signed kernel blobs or a compatibility matrix we can guarantee. Can we sketch a path? :thinking:

alex (eng-runtime): Short answer: yes, but pinning is a freight train. We should try to automate compatibility verification + signed-artifact delivery first. Pinning loses flexibility for rollouts.

todd (platform): @alex fair but marketplace / SI customers often demand deterministic images. If we provide a small set of vendor-certified tags (e.g., rwinf/acme-a100:driver-525-cuda12.2-signed) that's acceptable. Need release gating and canary window.

jia (partner-eng): ACME specifically asked for: signed kernel modules (they validate signatures w/ their KMS), a manifest csv for our compat matrix, and a backstop hotfix plan if we hit regressions during their image certification. They also want an embargoed joint announcement timeline once certified.

ben (sre): FYI our nightly revealed a perf regression on CUDA 12.3 quant kernels for A100 after the latest runtime patch — job: infra/nightly/quant-regression-a100. Link: https://ci/redwood/jobs/infra/nightly/quant-regression-a100/1234 (failing on perf check). If we pin drivers to 525 for ACME, that should avoid this regression, but we need to ensure we don't double-ship regressions elsewhere.

maria (partnerships): Proposal: 1) Create a small "certified" channel of images for marketplace partners that are immutable & signed. 2) Add an automated compat CSV we publish to the partner registry. 3) If a regression is found, open a hotfix branch with a driver rollback or quick kernel re-sign. 4) Schedule a 48h canary for ACME before final push. Thoughts?

alex (eng-runtime): Sounds good. Operational details: we can generate the compat CSV during CI: header like `device,driver_version,cuda_version,kernel_version,signature_status,validated_on`. We should also run a trimmed compatibility test matrix: smoke (launch), perf sanity (p99 token latency sample), and model-infer smoke on a 2-step prompt.

code snippet (alex):
```
# build + sign + publish (simplified)
docker build -t gcr.io/redwood/ai-runtime:acme-525-signed-20260310 .
./tools/sign-kernel --kmod out/driver-525.ko --key /secrets/acme-hsm-key --out signed/driver-525.sig
gcloud artifacts docker push gcr.io/redwood/ai-runtime:acme-525-signed-20260310
gsutil cp signed/driver-525.sig gs://partner-artifacts/acme/525/
# generate compat CSV
./tools/generate-compat --image gcr.io/redwood/ai-runtime:acme-525-signed-20260310 > compat/acme-525.csv
```

todd (platform): Deployment flow notes: we need image immutability + marketplace tag freeze (no retag) and a manifest URL partner can fetch. Also ensure our release pipeline records the kernel signature fingerprint for audit.

jia (partner-eng): ACME will validate signatures using their KMS fingerprint. We need to deliver both the signature and the public key metadata. They asked for HSM-backed signing if possible — can we route signing through our KMS flow?

alex (eng-runtime): We can integrate with KMS/HSM; it's an ops change but doable. We'll gate it behind a feature flag for partners requesting air-gapped signing. Implementation plan: introduce `signing-service` that exposes a one-shot signing API used in CI. Logs recorded to S3 for audit.

ben (sre): About the regression: if canary fails we should have an automated rollback path. I propose branch `hotfix/acme-driver-525-rollback` that changes the runtime kernel module build back to previous ABI and re-signs. We should also add a smoke alert to SLO page so partner-eng sees signal immediately.

maria (partnerships): Comms plan: once ACME validates, we'll draft a joint release note. Suggestions: coordinate copy with @jia, schedule a comms freeze 24h before announcement, and set the announcement to go out after both legal and engineering signoff. Also decide who owns the public compatibility table. I'd nominate partner-eng to maintain per-partner rows.

jia (partner-eng): I can own the partner rows. I'll keep a living sheet and a published CSV. I want an automated job that updates the published CSV on successful CI validation.

alex (eng-runtime): I'll add a CI job `compat/publish-acme` that runs after the final gate. Job will: run quick tests, call signing-service, publish image and compat CSV. If anything fails, it posts back to the thread and opens `hotfix/` ticket.

maria (partnerships): Timing request from ACME: they want a certification window next week (Mon-Wed). That gives us 6 days to get the first canary image ready. Can we hit that?

ben (sre): We can if we freeze changes to the runtime stack today and prioritize the canary job. Need owners for: signing-service (alex), CI wiring (todd), partner CSV + comms (jia), rollback doc (ben).

alex (eng-runtime): I can start signing-service PR today. ETA for a minimal MVP: 48h.

todd (platform): I'll wire up the publish job and the tag freeze by EOD tomorrow.

jia (partner-eng): I'll prepare the partner CSV skeleton and the public manifest endpoint.

maria (partnerships): Great. Last bits: ACME asked that the marketplace image carry both the kernel signature and a SHA256 checksum of the signed blob in the manifest. Also they want an embargoed co-announcement — they recommended legal review first. I'll loop in legal after we have a green canary. :+1:

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: infra/canary/acme-image-20260311 starting at 2026-03-11T02:00Z. Notifying channel: @partners @sre.

ben (sre): I'll add the SLO smoke alert and an automated rollback playbook. Will link the runbook here after it's created.

maria (partnerships): OK — action items recap in thread: alex -> signing-service PR, todd -> publish job & tag freeze, jia -> compat CSV + manifest endpoint, ben -> rollback runbook + SLO alert. I'll update ACME with provisional schedule and embargo notes. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
